summary: search can read past Techmeme's first results page: --pages N (1-10) walks the archive's start=<offset> pagination 10 at a time, --start sets the first offset, records are renumbered and deduped by link across pages, and the walk stops at a short page or, with --days, once a page reaches past the window; the default single-page request is unchanged.
reason: The archive search returns only its 10 newest hits per request, so a windowed query for a busy topic (Microsoft over 30 days) saw a fraction of the month. A later page's failure keeps earlier pages and warns on stderr rather than failing the call.
validated_outcome: Live 'microsoft date:[10/16/26 TO 11/15/26]': 10 results on one page, 50 unique in-window results with --pages 5; 'microsoft --days 30 --pages 10' stopped early at 56.
